newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia set for Hanson-led revolt Borbidge says.
newsitem.headline: Australia set for Hanson-led revolt Borbidge says.

text.p: The Australian government faced an unprecedented revolt from the Right led by increasingly popular independent Pauline Hanson unless it extinquished native title, Queensland Premier Rob Borbidge said on Wednesday.
Borbidge said opinion poll results released late on Tuesday showing Hanson's One Nation party now had 10 percent support should serve as a warning to Prime Minister John Howard.

"I had warned the Prime Minister that unless we get a satisfactory outcome to the Wik solution, the very thing that we ard now seeing in the polls will be repeated in ballot boxes around Australia and we will see a revolt from the Right that
this country has never witnessed before," Borbidge told Australian Broadcasting Corp radio.
"The writing is on the wall for the Prime Minister. I indicated to John Howard last Thursday that that would be the likely political repercussion if he does not adequately respond to Wik," he said.
"If anything my position has hardened. I cannot commit to his package," Borbidge said after the poll results.
Another poll released on Wednesday showed that one in four voters would consider voting for the Hanson-led One Nation party.

An AGB McNair poll published in Wednesday's Sydney Morning Herald newspaper found that 25 percent of voters would be prepared to vote for One Nation in the lower house of parliament while 28 percent said they would consider voting for it in the Senate.
The poll was conducted last weekend.
The AGB McNair poll follows a Bulletin/Morgan poll released on Tuesday showing One Nation would attract 10 percent of first preference votes if an election was held now.

Howard has put forward a draft 10-point plan that he plans to legislate with or without the support of the various states, interest groups and aborigine, although he is continuing to discuss the details of the plan.
The plan falls short of the complete extinquishment demanded by Borbidge and the farm lobby.
